body:
**Starts** once #48 is merged.

## Why

On every turn, the model reads its system prompt and each tool's name, description, and input schema as one unit. That text is spread over several files, and some of it exists in no file in the form the model gets it:

- Tool descriptions and input schemas are in separate files, such as `src/tools/memory-tools.ts` and `src/tools/memory-input.schema.ts`.
- Some numbers are filled in from `settings.json`, such as "at most 300 characters." The coordinator's system prompt from #48 fills in numbers the same way.
- The input schemas are written in Zod, and the model gets the JSON Schema that Zod makes from them. That step can add things the source doesn't show. Example: Zod gave every whole-number input a maximum of 9,007,199,254,740,991, which the model would read as a real limit.

So comparing two versions of what an agent is told, such as before and after a change an evaluation (#53) tests, means reading diffs in several files and working out the final text by hand. This issue writes what each agent sees into one checked-in file per agent. A PR's diff of that file is the change to what the model sees, with the numbers filled in and the JSON Schema as the model gets it.

## Design

- [DEVELOPMENT.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT.md), sections 2 and 5.

## Open questions

None yet.

## Do

- Add a test that builds what each agent sees, and compares it to that agent's checked-in file, such as `coordinator.view.md`. The coordinator is the only agent so far. The file has the agent's system prompt, built with the real `settings.json`, then each of its tools: name, description, and input JSON Schema. Get the tools through an MCP client, as the `trip` and `memory` server tests already do, so the file shows them as the SDK gets them. Use Vitest's file snapshot (`toMatchFileSnapshot`), so a file that doesn't match fails the test and prints the lines that differ. A normal test run never writes the file.
- Add `npm run agent-views`, which rewrites the files. It runs only this test with Vitest's `-u`, so it never updates any other snapshot. The check stays in `npm run test`, so `npm run check` and CI fail on a stale file.
- Write both into DEVELOPMENT.md: the command in section 2, and in section 5, that a change to anything an agent reads, or to a setting it shows, comes with its rewritten view file in the same commit. Each issue that adds an agent adds its file to the test.

## Done when

- `coordinator.view.md` is checked in and shows the coordinator's system prompt and every tool it has, with numbers filled in from `settings.json`.
- Changing one tool description, without running `npm run agent-views`, makes `npm run check` fail with the changed line. Running it fixes the failure. Put the failure output in the PR.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.
